fixes.explanation: That's the finish line verse 1 sets: “…until her righteousness shines like a bright light, her salvation like a blazing torch.” Until then, the speaker won't keep still. That is a LOT of not keeping still. My mustache gives out after one batch of cookies.
This one's false, friend. Verse 6 says of the watchmen, “they will never be silent day or night.” That's the night shift with no quiet hour. I'd be asking where the break room is.

Harvest does come up in this passage, but it's in verse 9 and it's a separate promise. It isn't what verse 7 names. The stopping point for those who call on the LORD is there: “…until He establishes Jerusalem and makes her the praise of the earth.” So the answer sits in verse 7, not verse 9.

Verse 9 says it: “For those who harvest grain will eat it and praise the LORD, and those who gather grapes will drink the wine in My holy courts.” The ones who did the work get the meal. And they praise the LORD. I'd call that a good setup.

Kings do get a mention in this passage, in verse 2, where they see Zion's glory. But the road in verse 10 is for somebody else. It says, “Go out, go out through the gates; prepare the way for the people!” The people are the ones named.
No army is mentioned, friend. Verse 10 says, “Go out, go out through the gates; prepare the way for the people!” The word there is people, not army. The highway is for the people.

Verse 10 ends with the call to “raise a banner for the nations!” A banner is made to be seen, so I think the nations are meant to look at it. Nations came up in verse 2 too, where they see Zion's righteousness.

The holy courts are in verse 9, where the wine is drunk. This proclamation reaches a lot further. Verse 11 says, “Behold, the LORD has proclaimed to the ends of the earth…” That's much bigger than the courts.
Verse 12 says, “…you will be called Sought Out, A City Not Forsaken.” Sought Out is the opposite of left behind. Forsaken had a good run, but the name changes.
